voices.note: the mishna of ear blemishes, 37a.15 (same id as bekhorot_37a_al_elu_mumin_ozen)
the mishna of the gums, 39a.10, cited אלמה תנן at 37a.20
anonymous redactorial voice of this unit
the baraita on Lev 27:11, cited דתניא at 37b.2-4

props.gloss_en: the mishna: for these blemishes one slaughters the firstborn -- its ear damaged from the cartilage
the mishna: but not [damage to] the skin
the mishna (39a): the outer gums that were damaged or scraped, and the inner ones that were uprooted [are blemishes]
it is also written 'if there be a blemish in it' (Deut 15:21) -- [so blemishes beyond lame and blind are included]
'any ill blemish' -- it generalised again: generalisation, detail, generalisation -- you judge only what is like the detail
as the detail is explicit -- exposed blemishes that do not return -- so all exposed blemishes that do not return
the 'any' of 'any ill blemish' is an amplification
I require an 'ILL blemish', and [in a hidden blemish] there is none
[the exclusion of] a temporary blemish is from reasoning
now, we do not [even] redeem [consecrated animals] for it [a temporary blemish]
shall we slaughter [a firstborn] for it? -- [no]

'and if it be any impure animal of which they may not bring an offering to the Lord' (Lev 27:11) speaks of blemished animals that were redeemed -- since 'and if of the impure animal' (Lev 27:27) already states the actually impure animal (37b.3)
might they be redeemed for a temporary blemish? Scripture says: 'of which they may not bring an offering to the Lord'
[redemption is for] one that is not offered at all
this one is excluded, which is not offered today but [is offered] tomorrow
the baraita's conclusion: consecrated animals are not redeemed for a temporary blemish
